body.title: problem: The 2FA UI seems slightly confusing even for a technical person
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I was just trying to use 2FA on a new device with a different 2FA app, and ended up failing and then unintentionally deleting 2FA entirely even though I still would have it set up elsewhere.

### Problem description

The 2FA was confusing to me as a technical user and a long term 2FA user for multiple reasons:

- I tried to use the 2fa command line tool for *BSD systems with this, but the default setting of it isn't compatible, and Forgejo appears to show zero information about the algorithm and settings like hash etc. that is being used.

  I think the best way to deal with this would be to show this at the bottom of the page with a bit of a distance to the important code info, where a non-technical user won't be too confused by it.

- Also, trying to enroll my new device then having to cancel apparently just nuked 2FA entirely without a warning even though on my old device it's still setup. It's not clear to me if I need to re-enroll it now on my old device as well or what the state of that is. (Are all 2FA devices always in sync showing the same code? This isn't obvious to a non-cryptographer.)

  The more natural UI would be IMHO to either let me register each authenticator individually with a custom name, and/or add a "Cancel" button and then that button when pressed should e.g. at least explain the situation, e.g. that all devices are in sync and since I unenrolled I need to re-enroll all of them now, or I don't know.

### Potential workarounds

If somebody can think of better UI fixes then I'd be curious!

### Forgejo Version

_No response_

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

I use codeberg.org

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

body.title: problem: scheduled actions run against old commit (manual invocation runs against current commit)
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested locally with the latest development version)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I am managing a Forgejo instance for my art collective. I've only been using Forgejo for a few months, but I have experience with many other Git / version control hosts and CI runners.

Relevant to this issue, I am hosting an XBPS package repository in Forgejo. I have two Actions configured. One of the actions checks for upstream updates on a regular schedule, the other builds packages after a new commit has been made.

### Problem description

My ["autoupdate.yaml" Action](https://babel.heavendivided.net/HeavenDivided/void-repo/actions?workflow=autoupdate.yaml&actor=0&status=0) is running against commit `ac62564b0a` every time the cron schedule activates. This commit is out-of-date, and causes the action execution to fail.

If I run the workflow manually, it [correctly uses the latest commit](https://babel.heavendivided.net/HeavenDivided/void-repo/actions/runs/931/jobs/0/attempt/1).

This issue started after I upgraded to Forgejo 17.0.0. Prior to this update I believe I was running Forgejo 14.0.0, and the issue was not present. Scheduled actions [ran against the latest commit](https://babel.heavendivided.net/HeavenDivided/void-repo/actions?page=26&workflow=autoupdate.yaml&actor=0&status=0).

### Potential workarounds

The only workaround I have is to manually run the workflow periodically.

### Forgejo Version

17.0.0

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

Forgejo is running in a Docker container on a (shared) Ubuntu Server VM. Forgejo Runner is running natively on a dedicated Ubuntu Server VM. Both VMs are running under TrueNAS SCALE.

The Action in question is using the [void-glibc-full](https://github.com/void-linux/void-containers/pkgs/container/void-glibc-full) image.

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

body.title: enh: Automatically update task-list progress when linked issues change
body.body:
### Existing problems this enhancement addresses

Markdown checklists referencing other issues require manual synchronization. Closing a referenced issue does not check its task-list item or update the parent’s progress bar. Reopening it can likewise leave a previously checked item incorrectly marked complete.

For example, a parent issue with three linked tasks continued to display 0/3 after one referenced issue was closed.

Dependencies do not update checklist progress either. Maintaining both mechanisms duplicates tracking and allows their states to diverge.

### Enhancement description

Support issue-backed task-list items whose completion state and parent progress automatically follow the referenced issues:

- Closing an issue marks its item complete.
- Reopening it marks its item incomplete.
- Moving or transferring it preserves the relationship and updates the reference.
- Deleting it displays an explicit deleted state and adjusts progress according to a documented rule, without silently treating deletion as completion.
- Adding, removing, or replacing linked items recalculates completed and total counts.

Updates should work for changes made through both the UI and API. Ordinary checklist items without issue references should remain manually controlled.

This would provide a reliable parent progress bar with issue state as the single source of truth.
